entries.title: Newton's Three Laws of Motion
entries.content: 1st (Inertia): objects keep their state of rest/motion unless a net force acts. 2nd: F = m×a — force equals mass times acceleration (N = kg·m/s²). 3rd: every action has an equal and opposite reaction (rocket exhaust pushes ship forward). Foundation of classical mechanics.

entries.title: Gravity
entries.content: Newton: every mass attracts every other — F = Gm1m2/r². On Earth, g = 9.81 m/s². Weight = m×g (force) vs Mass (amount of matter, constant everywhere). Your mass on the Moon is the same; weight drops to 1/6 because g_moon = 1.62 m/s². Einstein reframed gravity as spacetime curvature (General Relativity).

entries.title: Electromagnetism Basics
entries.content: Moving charges create magnetic fields (electromagnets, motors) and changing magnetic fields create voltage (Faraday's induction — generators, transformers). Lenz's law: induced current opposes the change causing it (that's why back-EMF exists). Maxwell's equations unified electricity, magnetism and light — light IS electromagnetic radiation.

entries.title: Photosynthesis
entries.content: Plants convert CO₂ + water + light into glucose + oxygen using chlorophyll. Light reactions (in thylakoids) split water and make ATP/NADPH; the Calvin cycle (in stroma) fixes CO₂ into sugar. It powers nearly all food chains and produced Earth's oxygen atmosphere.

entries.title: Periodic Table Basics
entries.content: Elements are ordered by atomic number (proton count). Groups (columns) share chemical behavior — Group 1 alkali metals (reactive), Group 17 halogens, Group 18 noble gases (inert). Periods (rows) fill the same electron shell. Top essentials: H, C, N, O make ~96% of your body. Metals left/center; non-metals right.

entries.title: States of Matter
entries.content: Solid (fixed shape/volume, vibrating molecules), Liquid (fixed volume, flows), Gas (fills container, free molecules), Plasma (ionized gas — stars, neon signs). Transitions: melting/fusion, freezing, vaporization/boiling, condensation, sublimation (solid→gas, e.g., dry ice), deposition. Latent heat is absorbed/released during transitions without temperature change.
